ops.title: Pending-add stranded-dir leak: root cause, why naive daemon auto-reap is unsafe, and the safe design
ops.body:
## The leak (root cause)

`Store.SweepPendingAdds(cutoff)` (`internal/store/reserve.go`), called once per daemon start
from `daemon.Run` (`internal/daemon/server.go`), is a bare
`DELETE FROM pending_adds WHERE created_at < ?`. It frees the index reservation of an orphaned
add — a `ccp add` that died before `FinalizeAdd`/`AbandonAdd` — but **never tears down the
on-disk `~/.cc-pool/accounts/acct-NN` dir, its credentials (Keychain item + plaintext file), or
its overlay**. After the sweep the dir has zero references in either `accounts` or
`pending_adds` and nothing reconciles it → stranded permanently (this is how `acct-16` leaked).
The leak is minor (only a crashed-mid-add produces one; a few KB), so it was **shelved
2026-07-14** rather than fixed; revisit only if strandeds actually accumulate.

## Why the obvious fix is UNSAFE — do NOT just reuse `AbandonAdd` + a lease probe

A prototype (an `overlay_kind` column on `pending_adds` + `Store.StalePendingAdds` + a
`teardownPending` helper refactored out of `AbandonAdd` + `Manager.ReapStalePendingAdds` guarded
by a `SessionLeaseHeld` probe) passed the full suite, but **two independent codex (gpt-5.6-sol
xhigh) reviews REFUTED it as unsafe for an unattended daemon deleter**. Three disqualifying
defects (all real; #1 is non-speculative and sufficient on its own):

1. **No atomic claim of the pending row before teardown.** The reaper snapshots
   `StalePendingAdds`, then unconditionally tears each row down and does a bare-ID
   `ReleaseAccountIndex(id)`. `FinalizeAdd` is not transactional (`ConsumeAccountIndex` then a
   separate `UpsertAccount`), so it can promote index N to a **registered account** between the
   snapshot and the teardown → the reaper deletes the now-registered account's dir + creds, and
   the bare-ID release deletes 0 rows yet reports success. The same shape clobbers a `ReleaseAdd`
   deliberately-kept dir, and — worst — an **ABA replacement reservation** (a fresh `PrepareAdd`
   gap-fills N after the old row is consumed/released → the reaper destroys the *new* add's dir).

2. **Credential deletion happens outside any lease fence.** `teardownPending` deletes the
   Keychain item + file credential *before* `removeAccountDir`'s `ErrBusy` gate, and
   `SessionLeaseHeld` is an instantaneous **probe**, not a held lock. A live add that acquires
   its lease just after the probe — or that sits in the post-login/pre-`FinalizeAdd` window where
   interactive `loginFlow` has already *released* its lease — loses its just-written credentials
   irrecoverably (the dir may survive via the later busy gate; the creds are already gone).

3. **`overlay_kind` was persisted as DETECTED, not ESTABLISHED, and legacy rows default
   `symlink`.** A fuse→symlink Setup fallback leaves the row saying `fuse` → the reaper's FUSE
   provider `os.RemoveAll`s the deliberately-preserved `acct-NN.private` sibling
   (`convert.go`'s `removePrivateRootIfEmpty`/`HealStrandedPrivate` intentionally keep
   unclassified private data). Inversely, an old-binary row (no `overlay_kind` → reads back
   `symlink`) that actually established a mux-FUSE bridge → the reaper computes the wrong lease
   key (`ConfigDir` instead of `MuxRootDir()/acct-NN`), so the probe misses the live add and
   symlink teardown walks the live bridge. Data loss in both directions.

Downweighted (real but not drivers): the 32-bit `creds.ServiceName` SHA-256 truncation can
collide two acct dirs (≈0 for realistic pool sizes); a zombie/inherited-fd lease holder and a
persistent teardown failure are leaks, not data loss.

## Safe design (if the automatic reaper is ever built)

An autonomous daemon deleter needs ALL of:

- **Atomic ownership claim.** Give each reservation an immutable generation/token (column on
  `pending_adds`, carried in `PendingAdd`). Predicate `ConsumeAccountIndex` /
  `ReleaseAccountIndex` / the reap on `(id, token)`. The reaper must transactionally CLAIM a
  still-stale row into a `reaping` state (keeping the allocator-blocking row so N can't be
  re-reserved) *before* any destructive op, and make `FinalizeAdd`'s consume+upsert one
  transaction. A last-second recheck is just another TOCTOU — insufficient.
- **Fenced credential deletion.** Seize-and-HOLD the exclusive session lease across the *entire*
  teardown (symlink/FP: seize → delete creds → teardown → remove; FUSE: holder-delegated
  teardown → seize the now-plain path → delete creds/files). Never delete creds before the fence.
- **Established-backend persistence.** Persist `prov.Backend()` (the backend actually established
  after Setup/fallback), not the detected one. Reserve as an unclassified/`unknown` value the
  reaper SKIPS; UPDATE to the established backend after Setup completes (a kill-9 between setup and
  update leaves an unreapable `unknown` row — a leak, the safe failure direction). Legacy/omitted
  rows must also read back as the skip value, never `symlink`.
- **Registered-service guard.** Before deleting any Keychain item, refuse if a *registered*
  account claims that derived service (cheap defense-in-depth; also apply to `PrepareAdd`'s
  existing stale-cred purge).

**Alternative that sidesteps most of the above:** keep the daemon sweep index-only (safe) + add
detection that LOGS stranded dirs, and do the actual reaping in a **human-gated `ccp gc`** command
(a human won't run it mid-add; `gc` can refuse if any add is in flight).

## Decision (2026-07-14)

Shelved. The leak is minor; making autonomous deletion provably safe requires the allocator
change above on the hot add path — a poor trade for a rare few-KB leak. `acct-16` (the one known
stranded dir) was hand-cleaned (dir + db both clean; 15 accounts, no pending rows). The throwaway
prototype got the non-race parts right (schema, `StalePendingAdds`, the `teardownPending`
refactor, strict tests incl. a real lease-held skip) and is reconstructable from this doc.
ops.when: implementing pending-add reaping, or touching the cc-pool reservation allocator (ReserveAccountIndex/ConsumeAccountIndex/ReleaseAccountIndex/FinalizeAdd) or the daemon-startup pending-add sweep
